name: frog
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.

attributes.attribute: a magical being in Celtic folklore
carried a healing jewel on its head

text: The frog appears in Celtic folklore as a magical being. In Scottish tradition, a king frog carried a jewel on its head. The jewel held great healing power. A person could gain the jewel only by finding the king frog. The frog hid in a fen or a bog. The hunter lowered an otter into the water. The otter frightened the frog from its hiding place. The hunter then struck the frog on the head to dislodge the jewel. The seeker took the jewel before it slipped under the water.

okr.objective: The frog entry records the king frog and the healing jewel of Celtic tradition.
key_results: King Frog carried a healing jewel on its head.
The frog hid in a fen or a bog.
